bugs: DispatchCrmSync.php:22 iterates every unsynced subscriber each minute and runs a conditional UPDATE per row even when it is still claimed. During a queue backlog (symptom 2), that is one write per in-flight row per minute, all of which match 0 rows. It is not a correctness bug, but it is avoidable load.

The 15-minute claim TTL is shorter than a heavily backed-up queue can stay. A second job can still be queued, although the crm_synced_at guard in handle() stops the duplicate before it reaches the CRM. impl-2 has the same TTL.
antipatterns: tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:62-69: reads the #[Tries]/#[Backoff] attributes through ReflectionClass, which tests how the job is declared rather than how it behaves.
app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:11: the stale-claim TTL is a hard-coded public const, not config.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:104: the 1100-row chunk-boundary test for dispatch covers no reported bug and runs slowly.
The tests never run a real retry and failure through a worker; failed() is only called directly.
strengths: Finds all four root causes: the catch that swallowed exceptions (now removed, with failed() recording the error), duplicate dispatch, the scheduler's 24h default withoutOverlapping lock (now withoutOverlapping(10)), and chunk() skipping rows when the filtered column is updated (now chunkById).
An atomic conditional-UPDATE claim with a stale TTL prevents double dispatch while still re-queueing stalled rows.

Uses the Laravel 13 queue attributes Tries, MaxExceptions, Backoff and DeleteWhenMissingModels, sets Tries higher than MaxExceptions so overlap releases don't use up retries, and gives WithoutOverlapping an expiry and a release delay.
An idempotency guard in handle() skips subscribers that are already synced.

My database-queue probe confirmed that an outage leads to failed_jobs plus crm_last_error and then recovers on a later dispatch, that a backed-up queue sends one HTTP call, and that normalize processes every row.

bugs: The 15-minute requeue window can be shorter than a backed-up queue's latency, so a duplicate job can be queued. The crm_synced_at guard in the job stops it from reaching the CRM. impl-1 has the same issue.
antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:21 and :27: the stale-claim where-closure is duplicated in the select and the claim UPDATE. A local scope or a shared closure would remove the repetition.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:62-66: try { dispatch } catch (RequestException) {} swallows the exception with an empty catch, so the test doesn't show that the exception surfaces.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:99: the test name says it checks 'bounded retries', but it only checks the middleware properties.
Uses #[Signature]/#[Description] on DispatchCrmSync but leaves NormalizeSubscriberEmails with properties, so the two commands are inconsistent.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:7-8: imports are not in sorted order.
strengths: Finds the same four root causes and fixes them: rethrowing plus failed(), backoff, MaxExceptions with a higher Tries, an expiring WithoutOverlapping, a claim/stale requeue, withoutOverlapping(5) on the schedule, and chunkById.
Pre-filters claimed rows in the lazyById query, so in-flight subscribers aren't re-read and re-updated every minute while the queue is backed up.
Puts the CRM URL and requeue window in config/services.php (the code was already reading services.crm.url).
Uses modern Laravel 13 attributes: queue Tries/MaxExceptions/Backoff/Timeout/DeleteWhenMissingModels and console Signature/Description, all of which exist in the installed 13.40.

Includes a test that runs a failing sync through dispatch and checks the failed() side effect. My database-queue probe confirmed failed_jobs, recovery, one HTTP call under backlog, and full normalization.

v.rationale: The two implementations are almost the same. Both found all four root causes: the try/catch that swallowed CRM errors, re-dispatch every minute with no claim, the scheduler's 24h default withoutOverlapping lock, and chunk() skipping rows while it updates the filtered column. Both full suites pass (14 tests each). My database-queue probes behaved the same in both: an outage ends in failed_jobs with crm_last_error set and recovers on a later dispatch, a backed-up queue makes one HTTP call, and normalize covers every row. Neither has a real bug beyond the shared 15-minute TTL, which the job's idempotency guard mitigates. impl-2 ranks first for smaller reasons. It pre-filters claimed rows, so it doesn't issue one no-op UPDATE per in-flight subscriber each minute under backlog. It moves the TTL and URL into config. It uses console attributes and a Timeout. Its tests run a failing sync through dispatch to exercise failed() instead of reflecting on attributes. Against that, it duplicates the stale where-closure, has an empty catch in one test, and uses attributes on only one of the two commands. impl-1's reflection-based attribute test and per-row claim UPDATEs put it slightly behind.
